course_description:
Advanced Genome Informatics will equip students with the knowledge and practical computing skills necessary to undertake a wide range of genome scale analyses using data produced by high-throughput sequencing technologies. The background lectures will introduce current approaches for analysing data including read mapping, de novo assembly, visualization, and phylogenomics. There will be an emphasis in developing good practice in experimental design and understanding the principles that underpin the commonly used bioinformatics analysis tools. Throughout the course students will learn practical genomics in a series of computer-based practicals using real sequence data, unix command-line tools and high performance computing resources.

Each week, you'll participate in combined lecture/practical workshops built around sequence-data exercises using dedicated high-performance computing resources, ensuring you gain hands-on experience with established genomic analysis methods. No prior knowledge of the Unix command-line environment is needed as we start from the basics and build your skills throughout the course. Through a series of four interactive modules, led by expert genomics researchers, you'll assemble a toolkit of skills and experience that you can directly apply to any future genomics project.

course_aims: Advanced Genome Informatics will equip students with the knowledge and practical computing skills necessary to undertake a wide range of genome scale analyses using data produced by next generation sequencing (NGS) technologies. The background lectures will introduce current approaches for analyzing genome and transcriptome data including read mapping, de novo assembly, visualization, and phylogenomics. There will be an emphasis in developing good practice in experimental design and understanding the principles that underpin the commonly used analysis tools.

learning_outcomes.description: Appraise the theory and practice of genome informatics and be prepared to apply these methods to address current problems in the field.
Compare the different types of available genomic and transcriptomic data and critique the general approaches used to analyse these.
Examine the principles of sequence alignment to the practical problem of mapping reads to a reference sequence.
Judge the approaches required for the analysis of metagenomic data.
Appraise the principles underpinning common de novo assembly approaches.
Explain the approaches required for phylogenomic analysis of sequence data.
Describe the approaches required for genomic analysis and functional annotation of human genomic sequence data.

assessment_details.task_description: This assessment item aims to provide students with an opportunity to connect practical and conceptual issues relevant to the course. SIX In-lab assignments, each related to one of the 6 module 1 and module 2 workshops (weeks 2-7) will be introduced during the related workshop session. These assignments are formative and will aid you in learning the key command-line approaches required for analysing high-throughput sequence data. Assignments include preliminary practical exercises that will be completed in class. A passmark will be awarded for an assignment by showing your tutor a genuine attempt at the preliminary exercises before leaving the workshop session. Each assignment also includes additional exercises that may be completed during the workshop session or in your own time. Answers to each workshop will be given before the beginning of the next workshop. As the assignments are formative in nature, no extensions or deferral is permitted. Understanding of the approaches and concepts covered by each assignment will be assessed as part of the final end-of-semester examination. Workshop absences You must complete 100% of the practical component of this course (Assessment Hurdles - under Additional Course Grading Information). If you cannot complete your timetabled workshop session because of circumstances beyond your control (e.g., illness), you must contact me by email and attach supporting documentation that covers the date of the missed workshop. Applications must be received within 24 hours of your practical session. Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Translation (MT) This assessment task is to be completed in-person. assessment_details.title: ASSESSMENT 3: Metagenome analysis
assessment_details.task_description: Students will analyse and interpret metagenomic sequence data in the context of real-world scenarios. Analysis will include sequence simulation, sequence quality control, taxonomic assignment, and annotation using both web-based and command-line tools. Students will prepare answers to a problem as well as a report detailing the bioinformatic analyses of a viral metagenome and a description of the viral community.
